notes_on_the_expectation.this_lane_re_derived_the_july_prediction: from this lane's own measured 2A = 113.05 on july (7ay's read of the 511 vector: gain 17.901, B 95.15) and the desk's B(10) = 62.10, the predicted gain is 113.05 - 62.10 = +50.95 against 40.3's +50.96 -- a 0.012 s2/row agreement on a figure neither side took from the other.  december and january are CONSISTENCY, not confirmation: their B(10) was solved FROM 40.3's predictions, so those two deltas are zero by construction and are recorded as such.
notes_on_the_expectation.an_observation_about_the_chaos_coefficie: solving B(K) = c + e/K from the measured B(5) and 40.3's implied B(10) gives e = 330.6 / 532.5 / 426.0 on july / december / january, against 357.7 / 580.1 / 468.7 computed naively from the member spreads as (s511^2 + s255^2)/(1 - 1/5).  The ratio is 0.924 / 0.918 / 0.909 -- uniform enough across three folds to be a systematic factor rather than noise.  What that factor is (a small positive correlation between members, or a bias in the spread-to-variance conversion) is surfacefit's member-split question; it is recorded here before the read so it cannot be fitted to the answer, and it is an OBSERVATION, not a claim and not a prediction.  CLOSED by surfacefit 40.3 (e0eef8a), and by NEITHER hypothesis this lane offered: a + b/K over all C(5,k) subsets is exact algebra (residuals 1e-13), a equals the mean pairwise inner product and b equals S_d/(1 - 1/5) -- this lane's own denominator -- so the ratio is exactly 1 - 2cov/(s511^2 + s255^2), the CROSS-LADDER covariance the paired design creates on purpose.  Measured corr +0.072 / +0.078 / +0.091 gives 0.928 / 0.923 / 0.909 against this lane's 0.924 / 0.918 / 0.909, and this lane re-derived the identity to four decimals (0.9282 / 0.9225 / 0.9093).  Because s511 is close to s255 the ratio reduces to about 1 - corr, so the 0.92 was reading the cross-ladder correlation directly.  The sign matters and it is the good one: a POSITIVE covariance makes the paired increment's chaos LOWER than independence would give, so the naive column overestimated it and the paired read is slightly better resolved than 40.3 would need it to be.  Neither member dependence nor a conversion bias; the floor a is untouched, so none of 40.3's predictions move.
